Thanks for the context, Ben. Quick guidance below — drafting notes and a concise clause you can share back with SunHorizon.

High level: we can accept a publicity clause but recommend a 45-day embargo as our standard compromise. We will accept 30 days only if the scope is tightly limited to: (a) placement on Redwood partner/customer pages and (b) joint press releases where both parties provide written sign-off prior to publication. We should avoid blanket marketing rights.

Suggested redline (language to paste into the Order Form under "Publicity / References"):

"Publicity and References: Customer hereby grants to Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable, worldwide right to use Customer's name and logo solely for the purpose of (i) listing Customer on Redwood's publicly accessible customer/partner pages and (ii) inclusion in a joint press release, provided that Redwood obtains Customer's prior written approval of any press release or testimonial quote. Either party may request an embargo period; absent such request, publicity may occur 45 days after the applicable announcement. If Customer requests a shorter embargo (e.g., 30 days), Redwood may accept provided the use is limited to (i) a small logo on Redwood's partner page and (ii) no additional promotional placements without separate written consent. Customer will provide logos in scalable vector format (SVG) and identify a marketing contact for approvals. Nothing in this Section will permit Redwood to imply endorsement of Customer's products or services beyond factual statements of partnership or customer status."
Other practical notes:
- Add confidentiality carveout language: "Information that is already public or approved for release by the disclosing party is excluded from the embargo."
- Testimonial approval workflow: require email approval from the named marketing contact on Customer's side; we should capture that email approval as sufficient sign-off.
- Branding constraints: logos used per Customer brand guidelines; no alteration, no re-coloring, and display size limited to a standard partner grid (we can include a short spec if marketing needs it).

Please confirm whether Redwood accepts 30 days limited to partner page (and we'll propose the 30-vs-45 fallback language above), or whether we want to insist on 45 days as a condition of broader usage. If approved, Ben please send back this redline and the redlined PDF.
